business_rules.statement: A blocker never destroys local data. Every message that blocks work states, in the worker's own words, that their work is saved.

A blocker never suppresses the on-device safety layer. Gates, deviation detection, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold continue under every blocker; the deterministic backbone has no off switch.
business_rules.applies_to: all blockers, emergency pause, all fallback contracts

business_rules.statement: A blocker never lets a worker override it. No gate in the application can be overridden by the worker it blocks.
business_rules.applies_to: all gates under either enforcement posture

business_rules.statement: A blocker states a specific condition, never a generic failure; generic phrasing is banned.
A blocker is a scope reduction, not a stop, wherever safety permits. The canonical shape is the parked run: the blocked run parks and the worker continues with their other assigned runs.
A blocker's resolution is a named human act by a named role, never an indefinite wait on one person; where the named role is unavailable the escalation default applies, marked as a fallback delivery.
A notification is never the only mechanism enforcing a blocker. Every blocker is enforced by the device's own evaluation; the notification tells a human, it does not create the enforcement.
business_rules.applies_to: holds, qualifications, authorizations, approvals, suspensions, device commands

business_rules.statement: Cached credentials and qualifications are trusted offline within a bounded window: tenant-set, default approximately 24 hours, platform ceiling 72 hours; a tenant may shorten it, never exceed the ceiling.
business_rules.enforcement_point: on-device authority checkpoint; console cache-validity rule

business_rules.statement: A sync is forced before designated high-risk actions, sign-offs foremost, so the identities and authority those actions record are fresh, not stale cache.
A qualification clearance carries a tenant-defined duration; its expiry is enforced at the next gate evaluation and the platform does not yank a worker out of the step under way.
The clearance duration is set at tenant level and applies uniformly, deliberately not per-user.

The device renders what the package carries and never improvises. A missing specification limit cannot be guessed, a missing severity mapping cannot be defaulted, and a missing gate rule cannot be waived.
Specification gates are hard, always, for every tenant, and at least one severity mapping is required per measurement screen.
Each run is pinned to its package version; an in-flight run is never rebased.
Media is evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, never on the strength of an attempted upload; no unsynced evidence may be discarded to make room.
The login is the credential, not the device; a shared tablet confers nothing by itself, and attribution follows the login, never the device.
Where no supervisor is available a higher authority may sign off in their place, recorded in full — who signed, in lieu of whom, and why — with a notification raised, never a silent skip.

Evidence is immutable at creation, bound to the step, the unit where one applies, the worker's identity, the device and both timestamps, and cannot be edited after capture; a correction is an appended entry carrying who, when and what changed.
Captured media stays in the application's encrypted store and never touches the device gallery.

The Severity 1 floor is platform-fixed: automatic freeze of the breaching scope, Quality-Manager-only release, plus escalation; the freeze lands on the Lot, else the Unit for serialized work, else the Run with its output quarantined.

A hold placed on-device is in force locally at once; sibling devices learn at their next sync and the Command Center presents propagation honestly as issued, then propagating, then in force per device.

The command channel carries exactly five classes: lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, suspension, and version change; the device end is pull-based and commands are applied in order at each sync.
There is no real-time remote control of a worker mid-run.
No surface shows a command as applied because the server created it; command states are distinct throughout.
Skew-flagged writes cannot win a conflict unreviewed and are excluded from Resolve All; nobody may bulk-accept a skew-flagged entry, including the Quality Manager.

A conflict whose two values disagree beyond the screen's specification limits is passed to the rule-based deviation mechanism, because two materially different readings of the same capture is a quality event, not bookkeeping.
Resolve All produces one audit entry per conflict acceptance, never one for the batch, and each acceptance is individually transactional.

Late captures inside the record-finish window fold in flagged late_arrival; after finish, arriving captures follow the audited-recompute rule, never a silent rewrite, and scheduled reports flag material corrections in their next delivery.
The platform default for materiality is any change to a severity count.

Worker personal data anonymises at 24 months for standard commercial tenants, with measurement, result and evidence surviving and the identity becoming an opaque worker identifier, and never in Regulated-Industry mode; anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act.
Nothing is purged; the long-horizon record is owned upstream under a hot-retrievability horizon defaulting to fifteen years, beyond which data tiers and remains retrievable.

Worker safety outranks everything; the fixed priority order is worker safety, tenant isolation, security, authorization, qualification, specification and evaluation controls, approval and release authority, data integrity, auditability, controlled continuity, clear user communication, recovery and reconciliation.
Protecting a lower priority item at the cost of a higher one is refused; a proposed degraded mode must pass both the prohibition test and the priority test before it may be entered.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen: every administrative or operational change commits with its audit event in the same transaction.
business_rules.applies_to: all server-side mutating actions including root-initiated ones

business_rules.statement: Cached authority never widens: an offline device may do exactly what it could have done at the moment of caching, minus anything since revoked and reached the device, and nothing more.
A request whose authorization cannot be evaluated is refused, never permitted — fail closed.
Severity ambiguity resolves upward, never downward: where bands overlap the most severe applicable band is applied.
No decision item is ever auto-approved on timeout; absence escalates, it never auto-approves, and delegation is out of V1 scope.
business_rules.applies_to: all approvals, releases and gate items

business_rules.statement: A dead-lettered item is never discarded; purging the queue, auto-discarding aged items, or treating dead-lettered work as completed are all blocked.

No deployment or migration may disable any of the six enforced invariants — evaluation gate, sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, cross-tenant analytics anonymisation, one-transaction audit guarantee.
The tenant-configuration registry rejects rather than logs a looser-than-floor value, at the point of entry, with the bound stated.

No worker-facing text is ever machine-translated at runtime, in any blocker path; the Spanish variant comes from the versioned locale file and a locale-completeness check blocks publication in an incomplete locale.
The compliance-suspension worker message is quoted verbatim and is not open to rewording: "Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved."
The Frontline Worker Application never surfaces a sync conflict to a worker in any state; conflict resolution is a Command Center surface.
No worker-facing pace, timer against expectation, or comparison to others appears in any module, any state and any release.
No erasure occurs without a preceding final sync attempt being made and its outcome recorded; de-authorising a device must not destroy unsynced work.
The Training Library is excluded from the offline run bundle, is online-only by design, is never required mid-run, and nothing in a run depends on it.
Salvage always precedes any repair, rebuild or reset of a corrupt local store; unreadable records are dead-lettered with identifiers retained and the loss made explicit and audited.
Ordering at sync is authoritative by server receipt in every case, skewed or not; device timestamps never win ordering authority when flagged.
A run's production date resolves to the shift's nominal date, not to the calendar date of each capture, so clock skew cannot move a run between production days.

Every functionality specified anywhere in the blueprint cites an FB-* identifier; a specification that cites none fails review, and an unconfigured dependency failure routes to a controlled hold under FB-PLAT-004.
A controlled hold has no time limit and no automatic expiry anywhere on the platform, because an automatically expiring safety stop would be a safety stop that expires.

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run parks; where the whole workflow depends on the screen the run is cancellable with a categorised reason
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked run, no unchecked measurement recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A republished package carrying the limits, adopted at the next run boundary; the in-flight run is never rebased

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing evaluation evidence for agent-derived content at staging and run open
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Authored work instructions, already present in the package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the authored instructions are also absent, OFF-BLK-27 applies
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run continues on approved authored content only
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The content passes evaluation and republishes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing approval on package content — no completed Author, Reviewer, Release Authority record
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Approved content substitution
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run parks
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked run or reduced content, both with approved material only

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing safety rules — the package lacks gate rules, deviation-detection rules, or deterministic checks
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None. This is the one content blocker with no degraded mode
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — there is no fallback to fail; the terminal state is entered immediately
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run unstartable; no capture possible; other work unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A republished package carrying the safety rules

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Broken peripheral at scan invocation where the hardware scanner does not respond
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The camera, per §7.8.2
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the camera is also unavailable and the screen requires identification, the run parks
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked run, no fabricated identity, no unidentified unit recorded as identified

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Lost encryption key — the application-managed encrypted store cannot be opened at application start
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None for the unsynced data. The register's one genuinely unrecoverable entry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — there is no fallback to fail
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The loss is named, bounded to the unsynced set, audited, and the worker is productive on another device within minutes
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device re-enrollment with a fresh store; the lost captures are not recovered

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Clock drift beyond the tenant threshold, detected at sync per §36.4
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Order by server receipt, authoritative for ordering at sync in every case
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the server time source is itself in doubt, no write is granted ordering authority from device time and every conflict in the window routes to human review
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: All captures accepted, ordered by server receipt, flagged, reviewable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device time correction; the flag persists on historical writes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Queue corruption at protocol step 14
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Rebuild the queue from the store, the single on-device source of truth, then upload with idempotency and deduplication at steps 17 and 18
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Offer every store record in dependency order and let the server's idempotency guard prevent duplication
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Captures preserved in the store; upload deferred; nothing duplicated and nothing lost

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Multi-device conflict at protocol step 23 per §36.3 — the one blocker with no worker-facing message, deliberately
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Object-specific automatic resolution per the §36.3 authority table
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Human resolution; where values disagree beyond the screen's specification limits, escalation to the rule-based deviation mechanism as a quality event
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Both versions retained; the safer version carried; work never blocked

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Long-duration outage measured against three independent horizons: 30/60/120 minutes, ~24-hour trust window (72-hour ceiling), 48-hour record-finish window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continued offline execution
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Trust-window expiry, then OFF-BLK-08
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Runs continue to completion where the trust window allows; runs park or stop where it does not; every capture preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing authorized human at a step requiring a second-identity step-up with no authorised second identity present
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A substitute sign-off by a higher authority, recorded in full — who signed, in lieu of whom, and why — with a notification raised
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no substitute is present the run parks; the worker continues other runs
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked run, unsigned step, no forged or self-signed authorisation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A supervisor or substitute attending the device and signing

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Artificial intelligence unavailable — no connectivity, emergency pause, degraded reasoning service, or an opened circuit breaker
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Authored work instructions from the package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: OFF-BLK-27
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform's quality guarantee intact and local; guidance approved and present; the reasoning layer honestly absent
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Connectivity, service restoration, or an audited resume from an emergency pause

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Cached guidance unavailable — neither the agent card nor the step's authored work instructions are present
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None within the step. The true floor of the guidance chain
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — the terminal state is entered immediately
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked run; no uninstructed capture

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing severity action bundle or containment checklist, at staging and at classification time
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Severity 1 platform floor — automatic freeze, Quality-Manager-only release, escalation — applies regardless of any tenant bundle
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the containment checklist itself is missing, the run is unstartable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run unstartable, or running with floor-only severity behaviour and a recorded gap

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing locale rendering for the worker's language, detected at screen render
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Render the authored language that exists, stated plainly to the worker; nothing machine-translated at runtime
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no authored language variant exists at all, OFF-BLK-27 applies
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run continues in an authored, approved language, with the gap visible
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A republished package carrying the missing locale

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing work-instruction difficulty level for the worker's profile, at screen render
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The nearest authored level, preferring the more detailed one, because more guidance is the safer error
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no level exists, OFF-BLK-27 applies
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run continues on approved authored instruction at a stated level; no level is generated on the device at runtime

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No holdable scope for a Severity 1 hold — the breaching capture resolves to no lot and no unit
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Run-level freeze itself, which is the fallback branch
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — the Run always exists, so a target is always available
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run held, output quarantined, containment executed locally, release reserved to the Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Quality Manager disposition and, where appropriate, a lot-release command at the next sync

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Pending remote wipe on an unreachable device — command in a pre-delivery state beyond an expected interval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Wait for the device, holding the command in its honest pending state
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: DEC-WIPE-001 — the source states no pending horizon and no never-returns behaviour; both readings preserved, neither adopted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Command pending, not applied, honestly rendered; no surface claims an erasure that has not happened
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The device returning, or a client decision under DEC-WIPE-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Forced-sync-required action attempted offline (sign-offs foremost)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Park and continue elsewhere
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the whole shift is offline and every run ends in a sign-off, the runs park at their final step and complete after reconnection, well inside the record-finish window
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked at the sign-off step; every prior capture recorded and preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missing part reference for a consumption step, at screen render and capture commit
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Proceed with the step and record the consumption gap explicitly
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the authored configuration makes the part reference mandatory, the step blocks and the run parks
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The step's quality captures are recorded; the consumption reference is recorded as unresolved, never fabricated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The parts registry resolves at the next sync; an append-only correction adds the resolved reference

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Training Library unreachable — navigation to the library while offline
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The step's authored work instructions; nothing in a run depends on the library
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — nothing in a run depends on the library, so there is no work to fail
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: All runs fully executable; the library simply absent

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Substitute-authority hierarchy unresolvable offline at a substitute sign-off attempt
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The cached eligibility of the run's own supervisor of record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Park
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked run; no unverified authority recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Connectivity, or the supervisor of record signing

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Version-change command pending without its staged package, at step 22 and the next run boundary
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Stage the package at the next connection and apply at the following run boundary
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated staging failure surfaces in fleet telemetry and notifies the Tenant Admin; work continues on the pinned versions throughout
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: All runs execute on fully staged, pinned versions; the pending change waits

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device offline — sync failure or heartbeat lapse
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continue fully offline on the pinned work package; commit captures locally; queue uploads durably
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the local store cannot commit, FB-CAP-001 takes over; if the store is full, FB-CAP-002 and DEC-STORE-001 apply
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Device continues executing with all gates enforced; nothing uploaded and nothing claimed to be uploaded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on link restoration following the reconnection workflow

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Site offline — loss of every heartbeat from a Site
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Every device runs FB-NET-001 independently; the board degrades to last-synced with age
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the outage outlasts the offline credential trust window, FB-AUTH-004 governs
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Devices execute on pinned packages until their trust windows expire, then new sessions are refused

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Slow link — latency above threshold for a sustained period; the most deceptive failure in the family
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded retry with back-off; prefer resume over restart for partial transfers
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Treat as offline and enter FB-NET-001 rather than allowing indefinite slow operation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device is declared offline and behaves as offline; ambiguity is resolved toward the honest state

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Flapping link — state changes exceed the damping threshold in a rolling window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Damping: a stability period before declaring up, hysteresis before declaring down
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Suspend automatic sync attempts for a cool-down period and continue offline
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Stable offline operation with a single, unchanging user-facing state

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Capture upload interrupted — transfer terminated before completion
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resume the transfer from its last confirmed offset rather than restarting
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Dead-letter the capture with its full payload retained on device and server, raised for human attention
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capture remains committed locally and visibly pending; it is never marked uploaded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Evidence media upload fails, is oversized, or fails validation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry with resume; validate locally before the next attempt
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Quarantine the media server-side and raise an evidence-gap item to the Quality Manager; the measurement remains valid
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Capture recorded, evidence gap declared, media preserved locally pending manual retrieval
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic upload on connectivity or storage availability

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Lost upload acknowledgement
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Idempotent re-send; the server returns the original acknowledgement rather than creating a second record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the idempotency store cannot answer, the capture is quarantined for human comparison
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: One record, or one quarantined item awaiting a named decision; never two and never zero

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command undelivered — remains in a pre-delivery state past its expected window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command waits durably in the queue; delivery retried at each sync opportunity in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Per-class expiry under DEC-FB-003 with the issuer notified and a replacement decision required
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The pre-command state persists — a held lot stays held; an undelivered suspension means the device is still operating and every surface says so
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery at next sync in order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command delivered but unacknowledged past the expected window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-deliver idempotently; the device re-acknowledges without re-applying
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalate to the issuing role with the honest state "delivered, application unconfirmed" and require a human decision
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform treats the command as unconfirmed and every surface displays it as unconfirmed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command expired per the expiry policy
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Expire the command and notify the issuer with the reason and the device's last-seen time
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the issuer is absent, FB-HUMAN-001 applies and the decision escalates by role, never by individual
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No command in flight; the pre-command state persists; the record shows expiry explicitly
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-issue by decision — never automatic re-issue

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command superseded — a newer command of the same class targets the same object
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Mark the earlier command superseded before the newer becomes available for delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If both were delivered the device applies in order and the later wins deterministically; ambiguity escalates to the issuing role
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: One effective command, both decisions preserved in the record
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not applicable — supersession is a normal control-flow outcome, not a failure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Identity provider unavailable, slow, or returning invalid assertions
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded retry, then present the failure honestly rather than falling through to a weaker credential
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Existing valid sessions continue until normal expiry; no new sessions are created
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No new administrative or staff sessions; the floor continues because worker PIN authentication does not depend on the tenant identity provider

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Token or session expiry, possibly during an unsaved action
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Silent renewal where connected; otherwise preserve the in-progress capture locally and prompt for re-authentication
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If re-authentication fails, the capture remains preserved and uncommitted, visible as pending
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No unauthenticated write; no lost keystroke

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Multi-factor authentication unavailable or the user's factor lost
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry; alternate enrolled factor belonging to the same person
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Access is refused; the compliance-emergency path exists for genuine emergencies and is a separate, louder, dual-authorised route, not a multi-factor bypass
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No access — a legitimate and expected outcome
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-enrolment through the platform's own administrative path by a different authorised person

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Offline trust window expiry, possibly with a run in progress
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Attempt authentication; any connectivity at all resolves the situation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Controlled stop with all captured work preserved locally; mid-run behaviour is DEC-FB-009 with both readings preserved
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device performs no further gated work and displays a sign-in requirement; captured work preserved and uploadable once identity is restored

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Authorization service unavailable or slow
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded retry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Fail closed — a request whose authorization cannot be evaluated is refused, never permitted; read-only degradation only for already-authorized sessions inside the cached validity period
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The surface is unavailable rather than permissive

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Role revoked while a device is offline
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The revocation is queued on the command channel and applied at next sync, in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where urgent, the suspension command class or a device de-authorisation is used, subject to DEC-WIPE-001
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Exposure bounded by the trust window; every interim action attributed and fully audited; no retroactive invalidation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Qualification expired or unverifiable offline at a gate
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Strict posture: the step blocks and the run parks; notify posture: the step proceeds and the signal is recorded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no supervisor is reachable, FB-CONT-004 and FB-HUMAN-003 govern; the run stays parked and may be reassigned
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Parked run; other work continues; nothing unqualified performed under strict posture
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Clearance at sync, reassignment, or requalification recorded in the Hub

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Work package missing on the device at run start
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Download or resume download where connectivity exists
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Reassign the run to a device that holds the package, or bring the device online
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run does not start on that device — the clearest example on the platform of a controlled stop being the correct answer

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Work package corrupt — integrity verification failure at load
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Skips Level 1 deliberately and enters at Level 3: discard the corrupt copy and re-download a verified copy
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run does not start, exactly as in FB-PKG-001
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No execution on that device against that package; no part of the corrupt package is used

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Work package expired — the required adopted version is absent for a new run
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Download the adopted version for the new run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Reassign the new run to a device holding the adopted version
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: In-flight work completes correctly on its pinned version; new work waits

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Work package incompatible with the device or application version
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Prompt for an application update where connectivity permits
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run does not start
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No execution on an incompatible device; no partial rendering of a gated screen

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Work package revoked, possibly reaching a device mid-run
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deliver the revocation on the command channel; it applies at next sync in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: DEC-FB-012 open — pinning wins and the run completes flagged, or safety wins and the run stops as a controlled hold; recommendation is to stop the run
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Under the recommended reading the run is stopped with all captures preserved and the reason recorded; under the pinning reading the run completes flagged for mandatory Quality Manager review
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Replacement version published through the full approval chain; no shortcut exists

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Capture cannot be committed locally — storage full, storage fault, encryption failure, partial write
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the local write; free reclaimable non-essential local data such as cached coaching assets, never evidence
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run is stopped on that device and the Supervisor moves the work to another device via reassignment
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No false completion — a step is either captured or visibly incomplete
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device repair or replacement; work moves to a conformant device

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Evidence store full or unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reclaim non-evidence local data; prioritise upload of the oldest evidence
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Refuse new evidence capture and declare an evidence gap, preserving everything already captured
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No evidence deleted; new evidence-bearing steps blocked; measurements still recordable where the workflow permits a declared gap
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Capacity restored by upload and reclamation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Peripheral failure — camera, scanner or measurement peripheral fault, permission revoked, pairing lost, invalid data
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry initialisation; re-grant the permission; re-pair
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Move the work to a conformant device through reassignment
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The step is incomplete and visibly so; the run may be reassigned; no fabricated capture

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Deviation detection fails to run — rules absent, unreadable, runtime fault, or clock unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-load the rules from the verified package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Stop the run on that device; move to a conformant device. There is no manual substitute for the deterministic gate
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No capture is accepted while detection cannot run — evaluation failure blocks, it never passes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Severity classification fails or is ambiguous — mapping absent, value outside every band, catalog mismatch
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Apply the most severe applicable band; ambiguity resolves upward, never downward
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no band applies at all, treat as a deviation at the highest severity the tenant's catalog defines for an unmapped departure — DEC-FB-013 open; else block the step and stop the run
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Either a classified deviation with its floor actions applied, or a stopped run. Never an unclassified out-of-specification capture
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Corrected mapping published through the Author, Reviewer, Release Authority chain

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Hold placement fails — local write failure or no lot, unit or run identity resolvable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the local hold write
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalate the hold target upward: Lot, else Unit, else Run with output quarantined; if none, stop the run entirely and refuse further capture
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run stopped, output quarantined, Quality Manager disposition required
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Quality Manager release through the lot-release command class

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Hold propagation delayed or incomplete — sibling devices offline
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continued propagation attempts at each sibling's next sync
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Physical intervention by the Supervisor; where impossible, the tenant's own quality-hold practice outside the platform, recorded as a manual episode
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The breach point is protected immediately and locally; every surface states the true per-device position

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Containment checklist unavailable at classification time
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Fall back to the authored Work Instructions for the step
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant's standing quality procedure through the Supervisor; then stop the run and hold the scope
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Hold in place, run stopped, Supervisor engaged; nothing fabricated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Corrected package published through the approval chain

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Escalation undeliverable — both channels unavailable or the recipient device offline
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deliver on the other of the two channels; in-app cannot be muted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Fallback tiers in the escalation record; then physical escalation with the platform recording that electronic delivery failed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold stands. The deviation stands. The escalation is recorded as undelivered rather than delivered
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Channel restoration or fallback tier delivery

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No eligible recipient on shift — role resolution returns an empty set
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The configurable recipient list, then the Tenant Admin, who always exists — the structural guarantee that the escalation chain cannot terminate in nobody
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold stands and the escalation is queued; the deviation is never closed by the absence of a recipient
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A holder comes on shift or is assigned

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No authorized approver available; decision item ages past its timer
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalate to another holder of the same role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalate by the tenant's escalation record; then the item waits — waiting is the correct outcome
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The decision remains open and visible, the held object remains held, and nothing is approved by default or by timeout
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A decision by an authorised person

failures_fallbacks.trigger: In-application channel unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Email, the platform's other and only remaining V1 channel
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The notification remains durably queued and appears when the surface reconnects; then escalation by voice or in person, recorded afterwards
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Queued and visible on next surface load; nothing dropped; nothing marked delivered

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Email vendor unavailable, rate-limited, or provider-accepted but undelivered
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-app delivery, which cannot be muted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Durable queue with ordered de-duplicated replay; then escalation by voice or in person for safety-class items
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Everything queued, nothing dropped, every state honest, and the tenant told that email is degraded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Both notification channels unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Durable queueing of everything, with strict ordering and de-duplication
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Surface-visible standing states rather than pushed messages; then out-of-band human escalation, which is DEC-FB-006 open
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Every safety mechanism intact; every notification queued; every surface honest; nothing acknowledged that was not read by a person
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Either channel restored, with paced drain to avoid a notification storm

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Model provider outage — failover threshold reached
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Route to the fallback router role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Lightweight router role and semantic cache, each labelled in the trace; then declare the agent unavailable — no degraded output presented as a normal result
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agents unavailable; deterministic layer, gates, classification, holds, containment and Work Instructions all untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Provider restoration; the agent resumes on its next trigger

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Specific model outage or withdrawal, deprecation, or behaviour change under the same name
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Route to another model already evaluated for that capability
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Disable the capability and show it as unavailable while a replacement is evaluated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No unevaluated model serves any capability, at any time, for any reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Retrieval outage — index unavailable, stale, or embedding service down
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Serve from the last-known-good index with its freshness stated in the trace and decision record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Produce output without retrieval, explicitly marked as produced without prior-case context; then declare retrieval-dependent capabilities unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No cross-tenant retrieval under any degradation; no fabricated prior cases

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Memory outage across the five typed stores
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry; degrade to the memory types that are available and record which were missing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Run the agent with working memory only; then declare the agent unavailable rather than producing output whose context is unknown
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No agent output produced from an unknown memory state; deterministic layer unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Store restoration; memory rebuilt from the operational record where derivable

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tool or atom failure — handler error, timeout, invalid result, partial effect
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded retry for idempotent atoms only; non-idempotent atoms are not retried without a compensating action
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Replan as a first-class traced event; then agent unavailable. For a detection-class mirror atom the on-device classification remains the act of record
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No partial side effect left unrecorded; no agent output that depends on a failed tool

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Orchestrator failure — service unavailable, run stuck, run looping, trace write failure, incorrect replay
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Restart the run from its last stage-boundary checkpoint
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Abandon the run and record it as failed; then all agents unavailable platform-wide, rendered as unavailability rather than silence
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agents unavailable; raised gates stay human-decidable; the deterministic backbone continues untouched and has no off switch
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Service restoration; resume is a separate audited act where a pause was involved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Low-confidence output — no confidence threshold is stated anywhere in the source (DEC-FB-014)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Present the output with its evidence and let the human judge — agents propose, humans decide
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Withhold the output and state that no usable interpretation was produced; then agent unavailable for that item
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No proposal reaches a decision queue without its evidence; no low-quality output presented as authoritative

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Unsafe or out-of-policy output; uncurated content; prompt injection through worker free text or evidence captions
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Suppress the offending output and deliver nothing rather than something unbounded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Fall back to the authored Work Instructions; then disable the capability and raise a platform incident
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Only curated, approved content reaches a worker, always
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Bound correction, input sanitisation, re-evaluation through the evaluation gate

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Quota or token ceiling exhausted mid-shift
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Warn at the usage-ladder thresholds of 80, 100 and 125 percent before the ceiling is reached
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Degrade to the lightweight router role and cache; then agents unavailable for that tenant with the commercial conversation raised
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agent unavailability for one tenant; no cross-tenant effect; no safety effect
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Ceiling raised through the normal change path, or the allocation period rolls

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Emergency pause invoked as a critical-class action (a deliberate operator action, not a failure)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-flight agent runs checkpoint at their next stage boundary and park; raised gates stay human-decidable
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Per-tenant pause instead of platform-wide; if the pause cannot be applied, the capability is disabled at the routing layer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agents unavailable; floor safety untouched; every tenant Command Center showing an honest agents-paused-by-the-platform state
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume as a separate audited critical-class act

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Primary database outage — unavailable, slow, read-only, stale replica reads, partial transaction
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded retry; failover within the cluster where the deployment provides it
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Read-only degradation from a replica with every view labelled with its replication age; then refuse writes entirely
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Web surfaces read-only or unavailable; the floor continues offline-first; nothing written that cannot be audited
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Cluster restoration, then drain of device queues under back-pressure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Queue outage — enqueue failure, backlog growth, poison messages, consumer stall
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry enqueue; the transactional outbox retains the intent so a queue outage delays delivery rather than losing it
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Drain from the outbox in order with idempotent consumers; then dead-letter poison messages with full payload and history — never discard
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work delayed, never lost; ordering preserved where it matters; nothing marked delivered that was not

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Object storage outage affecting evidence media, packages, parts-registry data and training content
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry; serve from cache where a cached copy exists, with its age stated
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Defer evidence upload with devices retaining media; then declare evidence display unavailable rather than showing an incomplete set as complete
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing lost; evidence review paused rather than partially performed; devices holding their media

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Audit service unavailable — the structurally strictest contract on the platform
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded retry of the whole transaction, both the operational write and the audit write together
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: None that permits the action; refuse the action and tell the user plainly that it did not happen
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Server-side administrative and operational writes stop, including for the root account; the Frontline Worker Application continues because device-side capture commits locally

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Scheduler Controller unavailable — process down, leader election stuck, split leadership
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Standby Controller takes leadership under a lease with a higher fencing token
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Occurrences accumulate as due; then manual execution by platform operations for individually critical occurrences as an audited administrative act
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Occurrences pending and visible; no duplicate execution; no silent skip

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missed occurrence — due time passed by more than the schedule's tolerance with no completion
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Execute late, recording both the due time and the actual time
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Apply the Schedule Definition's misfire policy — catch up, skip with a recorded skip, or route to a human; then dead-letter
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Every occurrence has a recorded outcome, including "skipped by policy"; the finish window is anchored to the due time, not the execution time

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Duplicate trigger — two claims on one occurrence, split leadership, or retry without idempotency
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Fencing token rejects the stale writer so the second effect never lands
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Idempotency on the occurrence identifier suppresses the duplicate; then quarantine the ambiguous outcome and require a human decision before any irreversible step
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: One effect, or none plus a quarantined item; never two, and never an irreversible act taken twice

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Orphaned lease — lease expiry without completion after a worker crash or partition
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reclaim with a higher fencing token; the original worker's late writes are then rejected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Re-execute idempotently from the occurrence's start; then quarantine where the work is not safely re-executable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The occurrence completes exactly once, or is quarantined with a named owner

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Stuck execution — run duration beyond the schedule's expected band
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Time-bound the execution and abort cleanly, releasing the lease
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Split the work into smaller batches and re-run; then dead-letter with the partial state recorded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Bounded resource use; a recorded partial outcome; no silent half-finished lifecycle operation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Dead-letter growth — depth or oldest-item age beyond threshold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Alert on depth and age thresholds
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Human triage with re-drive of items whose cause is fixed; then escalate to platform leadership — deleting the queue is prohibited
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Items retained and visible until a human dispositions each one

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Single sign-on integration outage, including certificate expiry and metadata drift
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: As FB-AUTH-001 — bounded retry then honest failure
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Platform-managed credential path for staff without an identity provider; outage-time use by existing SSO users is DEC-FB-011
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No new staff sessions; the worker credential path is unaffected

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Email vendor integration outage, plus reputation-driven blocking and tenant-side mail filtering
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-app delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Durable queue and de-duplicated replay; then out-of-band contact by the client's platform team, subject to DEC-FB-006
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: As FB-NOTIF-002 — everything queued, nothing dropped, every state honest
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Vendor restoration and reputation recovery, which can be materially slower

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Enterprise-resource-planning stub called — a tenant integrating against it and expecting acceptance
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Return 501 consistently with a clear message naming V2 scope
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual run creation, the supported V1 path; there is no integration to fall back from
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The stub refuses; no partial integration behaviour exists; reserved fields stay null

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Approver absent, unreachable, the only eligible approver is the creator, or their role was revoked
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Another holder of the same role — segregation of duties is satisfied by any second holder
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalation by the tenant's escalation record; then the item waits, visibly, ageing
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing approved; the object stays in its pre-approval state — a Job stays pending_approval, a workflow stays a draft

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Quality Manager absent — single-holder tenant, weekend or holiday
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Another Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The nobody-on-shift default routes to the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift as a fallback delivery; then the lot stays held — there is no third party who may release it
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Held lot, held product, open request — the outcome that stands up in a quality audit and the intended one

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Supervisor absent — area coverage gap or shift boundary
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Another Supervisor with the relevant Area or Site scope
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalation to the Quality Manager role; then parked runs stay parked and workers continue their other assigned runs
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work continues where it can; blocked work stays visibly blocked; nothing granted without authority

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tenant Admin absent, sole Tenant Admin departed, or account locked out
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Another Tenant Admin
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The client's platform team assists only through the three named access classes; a support session is read-only and cannot make the change; the compliance-emergency path is not a convenience route for a locked-out Tenant Admin
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Configuration frozen; operations continue on the existing configuration; no ambient platform administration occurs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Tenant Admin is appointed or restored

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Root Super Admin unavailable — custodian unavailable, credentials lost, multi-factor device lost, custodian departs
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The custodian's own recovery path — alternate enrolled factor, allowlist adjustment through the platform's own controls
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not specified in the Statement of Work; DEC-FB-007 open. Critical-class actions wait: tier publication, compliance suspension, all-tenant broadcast, device wipe and de-authorisation, emergency pause and resume, erasure and archival execution, retention-value changes, legal-hold placement and release, severity-catalog changes and floor-register changes
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform runs; critical-class change stops; Admin-band and Platform-Engineer-band operations continue under maker-checker
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restoration or re-provisioning under the procedure agreed in DEC-FB-007

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Shift change during an open incident — brief not produced, brief unacknowledged, incident opened after generation, or the outgoing person leaves first
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The brief itself, acknowledged and annotated by the incoming Supervisor as Command Center action six
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The standing state on every surface — open deviations, held lots, ageing decision items and parked runs are visible on load; then escalate unacknowledged briefs and unhanded-over open Severity 1 items to the Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Holds persist; open items stay open and visible; nothing closes because a shift ended

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Regional outage in the single stated V1 region
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Multi-zone redundancy inside the region, which is what a single-region posture can offer
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The floor continues offline-first; there is no stated cross-region failover and none is invented — DEC-SPOF-001 open
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Server-side surfaces unavailable; the Frontline Worker Application executing offline until trust windows expire; nothing lost
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Regional restoration then staged reconnection with back-pressure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Deployment failure — failed deploy, partially deployed fleet, or a healthy deploy with a latent regression
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Automatic rollback on health-check failure
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual rollback by platform operations; then forward fix under an incident with the tenant told honestly
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The last known-good version running; the floor unaffected throughout because devices hold pinned packages
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rollback or fix; the six enforced invariants survive every deployment

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Data migration failure — partial migration, failure mid-flight, semantics corrupted, or an irreversible migration
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reversible migrations by design, applied in expand-then-contract order so old and new application versions can both run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Roll back where reversible; then restore from backup, accepting the Recovery Point Objective consequence, and reconcile device queues afterwards
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A consistent database at a known version, with every discrepancy recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rollback or verified restore plus reconciliation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Configuration failure — invalid value, unintended effect, configuration unavailable, or partial propagation. Also the default contract for any dependency whose own contract is missing
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Rejection at the point of entry with the bound stated
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Revert to the previous approved value; then fall back to the platform default and raise an incident
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A known, validated configuration in force; no service running on an unvalidated value
